title: Autoscaler prematurely scaled down dedicated capacity after short burst, causing request rejections
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
A high-value customer reported a sustained spike ~2026-03-04 that briefly exceeded their reserved throughput. Shortly after the spike subsided the dedicated autoscaler reclaimed capacity aggressively, terminating pre-warmed worker VMs and evicting queued requests. This led to a 5–12 minute window of request rejections and elevated latency for customer routes before fallback routing and emergency provisioning restored capacity.

Why this is unique: Unlike previous 'pool depletion' incidents, the root interaction is between our burst credit evaluation window, a short-lived GC pause in the autoscaler agent, and the reserved-pool scale-down heuristics which treat samples older than 30s as stale. The result was an early scale-down decision despite ongoing KV-cache warmup traffic that still required capacity.

Impact:
- Customer-facing errors: 4.8% 500s on dedicated routes for the affected tenant during the incident window.
- SLA blip for one enterprise customer; legal/sales notified.
- Internal paging and blameless escalation from on-call infra and solutions engineers.

Current state: Hotfix deployed to canary and customer tenant; awaiting rollout to all dedicated clusters. Post-deploy metrics show stable behavior in canary clusters.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated reserved pool with 8 pre-warmed workers and burst credit enabled.
2) Send a high qps burst for ~90s that forces short-lived additional ephemeral workers to be created.
3) Immediately after burst ends, trigger a short GC/pause on autoscaler agent (simulate CPU scheduling pause or high GC on agent process).
4) Observe autoscaler sample aggregation: outdated samples + observed decrease in instantaneous qps cause scale-down decision to remove pre-warmed workers within 30s window.
5) Confirm request rejections while KV caches are still warming on newly launched replacements.

2026-03-04 09:18 UTC - On-call infra joins Slack incident channel; triage identifies dedicated-reserved pool involvement.
2026-03-04 09:25 UTC - Emergency rollback of aggressive scale-down heuristic pushed to affected cluster as short-term mitigation.
2026-03-04 11:40 UTC - Root-cause hypothesis formed; small canary fix implemented and applied to customer tenant.

2026-03-12 10:02 UTC - Post-deploy review meeting; ticket moved to In Review pending code review feedback and ops runbook updates.
root_cause: Autoscaler scale-down decision logic used a short aggregation window combined with strict stale-sample eviction. A transient GC pause in the autoscaler agent caused a gap in metric sampling; the aggregator then over-weighted older (pre-burst) low-utilization samples and triggered scale-down that removed pre-warmed reserved workers while KV caches were still warming. Additionally, burst-credit accounting reset too aggressively during brief sampling lapses, making the system believe burst capacity was exhausted when it was not.
fix_implemented: 1) Short-term hotfix: Add a 60s 'grace window' after detecting an ephemeral worker termination event that prevents scale-down of pre-warmed workers for the same tenant (applied to customer cluster).

2) Autoscaler agent: Improve sampling resilience by tolerating one missed sample without immediate stale eviction and smoothing by exponential moving average over 45s.
   PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
3) Burst-credit logic: Change reset semantics to require two consecutive empty-sample windows before draining burst credits for a tenant.
4) Ops: New alert when reserved-prewarm count changes > 20% in 60s for any tenant (to detect aggressive reclaim).
validation: Canary cluster (us-west-2-dedicated-3) showed no 5xx spike after simulated bursts for 48h.
Load tests with KV-cache warmup show <0.2% rejected requests during scale events (previously 5-12%).
Wall-clock comparison of scale-down events before vs after shows median cooldown increased from 18s to 72s for tenants with recent ephemeral worker activity.

postmortem_actions: 1) Ship full autoscaler resilience improvements in runtime-1.22 (target: 2026-03-26).
2) Add a dedicated end-to-end test that simulates burst -> GC pause -> post-burst scale-down to CI load suite (ENG-25001).
3) Update runbooks: include steps for emergency rollback of scale-down heuristics and a list of signals to check (burst-credit, sampling-lag, prewarm-count).
4) Product: document limits and recommended pre-warm sizing for large customers and include in onboarding checklist.
5) Sales/CS: follow-up with affected customer to confirm credit applied and agree on SLA remediation plan.
